sn12.46:1.2: Then a certain brahmin approached the Blessed One and exchanged greetings with him.
sn12.46:1.3: When they had concluded their greetings and cordial talk, he sat down to one side and said to him:
sn12.46:2.1: “How is it, Master Gotama: is the one who acts the same as the one who experiences the result?”
sn12.46:2.2: “‘The one who acts is the same as the one who experiences the result’: this, brahmin, is one extreme.”
sn12.46:3.1: “Then, Master Gotama, is the one who acts one, and the one who experiences the result another?”
sn12.46:3.2: “‘The one who acts is one, and the one who experiences the result is another’: this, brahmin, is the second extreme.
sn12.46:3.3: Without veering towards either of these extremes, the Tathagata teaches the Dhamma by the middle:
sn12.46:3.4: ‘With ignorance as condition, volitional formations come to be;
sn12.46:3.5: with volitional formations as condition, consciousness….
sn12.46:3.6: Such is the origin of this whole mass of suffering.
sn12.46:3.7: But with the remainderless fading away and cessation of ignorance comes cessation of volitional formations; with the cessation of volitional formations,
sn12.46:3.9: Such is the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.’”
sn12.46:4.1: When this was said, that brahmin said to the Blessed One:
sn12.46:4.3: I go for refuge to Master Gotama, and to the Dhamma, and to the Bhikkhu Saṅgha. From today let Master Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”
